html:
The Chitimacha are a Native American people of southern Louisiana, living in the Atchafalaya Basin and the bayous west of the Mississippi delta. Their language is an isolate, related to no other known language.

They lived in towns along the bayous, fishing, gathering shellfish and farming, and were known for their baskets woven from river cane in fine double-weave patterns. In 1706 some Chitimacha killed a French missionary, and the French and their Native allies waged war on them until 1718. Many captives were sold into slavery. Their neighbours to the west were the Atakapa and to the north the Natchez.

Unlike most peoples of the region, the Chitimacha kept part of their land, and they still hold a reservation at Charenton on Bayou Teche. The last fluent speakers of the language died around 1940, and the tribe has since used old recordings and notes to teach it again.
